name: LT3755EMSE-2#TRPBF
title: 40VIN, 75VOUT LED controllers (LT3755, LT3755-1, LT3755-2)
summary: The LT3755 family are fixed-frequency, current-mode DC/DC controllers that run a high-current LED string as a constant-current load, switching a ground-referenced external N-channel MOSFET from an on-chip 7.15V supply. The LED current is measured on the high side with a 100mV full-scale sense threshold, so one part covers boost, buck mode, buck-boost mode, SEPIC and flyback converters. PWM dimming reaches 3000:1, the CTRL pin adds analog dimming, and the FB pin gives constant-voltage regulation and open-LED and overvoltage protection. The -1 option adds a SYNC input in place of OPENLED; the -2 option has the revised OPENLED behaviour.

notes: The temperature grade letter (E, I, H) appears on a label on the shipping container, not in the marking.

E grade: performance is guaranteed for 0°C to 125°C junction; the –40°C to 125°C range is assured by design, characterization and correlation with statistical process controls. I grade: guaranteed over –40°C to 125°C. H grade (LT3755H-2 only): guaranteed over –40°C to 150°C.
The main difference between LT3755 and LT3755-2 is how OPENLED behaves once FB has crossed the overvoltage threshold; LT3755-1 has SYNC in place of OPENLED.

pins.name: PWMOUT
pins.function: Buffered copy of PWM, driven from INTVCC, for a disconnect NMOS in series with the LEDs or a level shifter. It is also pulled low when FB rises above VFB + 60mV (typ), whatever PWM is doing. A FET with a gate cut-off voltage above 1V is advised.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Voltage-loop feedback, regulated to 1.25V (nominal) by the gm amplifier whose output is VC. Used for constant-voltage regulation or for open-LED and overvoltage sensing. While FB holds the loop, OPENLED pulls low; if FB is forced above the overvoltage threshold, OPENLED releases and PWMOUT goes low. Must not float; tie to GND when unused.

pins.name: ISN
pins.function: Negative side of the LED current sense resistor. Above 2.9V the LED current follows ILED = 100mV/RLED for VCTRL > 1.2V, or (VCTRL – 100mV)/(10 • RLED) for VCTRL ≤ 1V. Bias current about 25µA typ. Below 3V it feeds the short-circuit detector, which holds GATE at 0V while ISP exceeds ISN by more than 150mV (typ).

pins.name: ISP
pins.function: Positive side of the LED current sense resistor. Its bias current depends on VCTRL (see the bias-current curve). Feeds the short-circuit detector when ISN is below 3V.

pins.name: VC
pins.function: Output of the transconductance error amplifier; an RC network to GND compensates the loop, and a series resistor with the capacitor is advised for fast transient response. Goes high impedance while PWM is low, holding the switch-current demand for the next PWM high period.

pins.name: CTRL
pins.function: Sets the LED current sense threshold. From 0V to 1V the threshold V(ISP – ISN) is one tenth of VCTRL plus an offset; above 1.2V it stays at the 100mV full-scale value; between 1V and 1.2V it bends over from the line to the constant, reaching 98% of full scale at 1.1V. Must not float.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: 2V (typ) reference output that can source up to 100µA, meant to feed a divider into CTRL for analog dimming or for LED temperature limiting and compensation.

pins.name: PWM
pins.function: Low stops switching, idles the oscillator and disconnects VC from every internal load; PWMOUT follows it. Has an internal pull-down resistor. Tie to INTVCC when unused.

pins.name: OPENLED
pins.function: LT3755 and LT3755-2 only. Open-collector pull-down that turns on when FB is above the FB regulation voltage minus 50mV (typ); needs an external pull-up of less than 1mA. While PWM is low and the converter idles, the pin holds the state from the last PWM high period and updates when PWM goes high again. Can report an open-LED fault.

pins.name: SYNC
pins.function: LT3755-1 only, replacing OPENLED. Logic-level clock input that the oscillator locks to; RT is chosen for a free-running frequency 20% under the SYNC frequency. GATE turns on a fixed delay after each SYNC rising edge. A 50% duty-cycle clock is the intended drive, and PWM performs best with its rising edge at least 200ns before the SYNC rising edge. Ground it when unused.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft-start. An external capacitor sets the interval; a 10µA (typ) source pulls the pin toward an internal 2.5V rail. The pin lowers the oscillator frequency and clamps VC while it is low. It is pulled to GND by an undervoltage on SHDN/UVLO or by thermal limit.

pins.name: RT
pins.function: A resistor to GND sets the switching frequency (Table 1, or the frequency against RT curve). Must not float.

pins.name: SHDN/UVLO
pins.function: Shutdown and undervoltage input with an accurate 1.22V falling threshold. Below the threshold a 2.1µA pull-down is switched on, so the external divider sets the rising hysteresis; above it (up to 6V) the pin draws under 1µA. An undervoltage resets soft-start. Held at 0.4V or below, the device is off and VIN current is under 1µA.

pins.name: INTVCC
pins.function: Regulated 7.15V (typ) supply for the internal circuits, the GATE driver and the PWMOUT driver, taken from VIN. Bypass with 4.7µF close to the pin. May be tied straight to VIN when VIN never exceeds 8V.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input; decouple locally with at least 0.22µF close to the IC.

pins.name: SENSE
pins.function: Switch current input for the control loop. Kelvin-connect to the positive end of RSENSE in the MOSFET source; the negative end of RSENSE is Kelvin-connected to the IC ground plane.

pins.name: GATE
pins.function: Gate drive for the external N-channel MOSFET, swinging between INTVCC and GND. Held at GND in shutdown, fault and idle.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Exposed pad: the only ground of the IC, and the negative-side sense input for the switch current resistor. Solder directly to the ground plane.

notes: Note 1: Operating past these limits can destroy the device, and long periods at any of them can shorten its life and reduce reliability.
Note 3: With VIN below 6V, keep SHDN/UVLO at or below VIN.
Note 4: Internal switches drive GATE and PWMOUT to GND or INTVCC; never tie them to an external supply.

Note 5: Overtemperature protection guards against brief overloads; while it is acting the junction is above its maximum operating temperature, and running above that maximum continuously can degrade reliability.

circuits.title: 50W white automotive LED headlamp driver
circuits.description: Boost converter from an 8V to 40V input driving a 50W white LED string at 1A (100mV across 0.1Ω) at 375kHz. R3 and R4 on FB clamp the output if the string opens, M2 on PWMOUT disconnects the string during PWM off time, and a 332k/40.2k divider from VIN to CTRL reduces the LED current when the input is low.

circuits.title: 50W white LED headlamp driver
circuits.description: The same 1A, 375kHz boost headlamp driver, with CTRL fed from VREF through 16.9k and a 100k NTC thermistor to GND, so the LED current folds back as the thermistor warms.

circuits.title: 20W SEPIC LED driver
circuits.description: SEPIC converter with a coupled inductor that drives a 20W LED string at 1A from 8V to 40V, so the input can be above or below the 18V string. C4 couples the switch node to the secondary winding and D1. FB with 511k/25k clamps the output on an open string, the Schottky from GND to ISN limits fault current out of ISN, M2 disconnects the string during PWM off time, and CTRL is tied to VREF for full-scale current.

circuits.title: Buck mode 1.4A LED driver
circuits.description: Buck-mode converter: the LED string, RLED and L1 hang from VIN and the low-side switch M1 pulls the bottom of L1 down, with D1 returning the inductor current to VIN. Three white Luxeon K2 LEDs run at 1.4A (100mV across 0.068Ω) from 15V to 40V at 375kHz. A PNP (Q1) level-shifts the voltage across the string and C3 to the ground-referenced FB pin for open-LED protection. M3, a P-channel switch above the LEDs, is driven through M2 from PWMOUT for PWM disconnect.

parts.value: 3 Luxeon K2 white LEDs in series

circuits.title: Buck mode 500mA LED driver for 20kHz PWM dimming
circuits.description: Buck-mode converter at 800kHz from 22V to 36V driving a 16V LED string at 500mA (100mV across 0.2Ω), for 20kHz PWM dimming with regulated pulses down to about 1µs. The disconnect NMOS M2 sits between the LED string and L1; its gate takes PWMOUT through 0.22µF, with a 6V zener and 1M from gate to source, and two Schottky diodes with a 2200pF capacitor from GATE feed the gate node from M2's source. FB is grounded and OPENLED is unused.

circuits.title: 21W buck-boost mode with 250:1 PWM dimming and open LED protection
circuits.description: Buck-boost-mode converter from 8V to 36V: the output after D1 rises above VIN, and the 21.5V, 1A LED string returns from it through RLED (0.1Ω) to VIN, so ISN sits on VIN and ISP on the LED cathode. A P-channel switch M2 at the top of the string, driven by Q2 from PWMOUT, gives 250:1 PWM dimming. A PNP level shifter (Q1, 392k into 20.0k) brings the output voltage to FB for open-LED protection. A 549k/75.0k divider from VIN on CTRL lowers the LED current at low input voltage.

circuits.title: Buck-boost LED driver for automotive
circuits.description: Buck-boost converter from 6V to 36V for a 1A LED string: an LTC4440-5 high-side driver, with its input on GATE, switches M1 from VIN to the inductor while M2 switches the far end of the inductor to ground through RSENSE, and D1 feeds the output. D2 runs from GND to the M1 source node; a Schottky from INTVCC and a 0.22µF capacitor to the M1 source node make the driver's BOOST supply. FB takes a 1M/40k divider from the output, CTRL a 383k/47k divider from VIN, and a PWMOUT-driven NMOS disconnects the string.
notes: Misprint: the inductor value is marked 22µF; it should read 22µH.

operation.text: Each oscillator cycle sets a latch that turns the external MOSFET on. The switch current, seen as a voltage across the resistor between SENSE and GND, is summed with a slope-compensation ramp and compared with the error amplifier output VC; when it crosses VC the latch resets and the switch turns off until the next cycle. VC is the integrated difference between the LED sense voltage V(ISP – ISN) and the target set by CTRL, so it sets the peak switch current that holds the LED current. All drivers and internal loads run from INTVCC.

The SENSE voltage may not pass the 108mV (typ) current-limit threshold; reaching it resets the latch whatever the PWM comparator says. When the ISP/ISN common-mode voltage is below 3V, an ISP–ISN difference above 150mV (typ) does the same, keeping GATE low until the difference falls. Together these protect the switch and the other power-path parts.

With PWM low, GATE and PWMOUT sit at GND, VC goes high impedance so the compensation capacitor keeps the last switching state, and the ISP/ISN bias currents drop to leakage. When PWM rises, PWMOUT follows after a short delay and the oscillator restarts at once. A disconnect switch in the LED path, driven by PWMOUT, keeps the output from discharging during the off time. Regulated LED current pulses as short as 1µs are reached in the 20kHz buck-mode application; the best mix of PWM and analog dimming comes with PWM pulses of at least six switching cycles. Dimming ratios reach 3000:1.

Above 1.2V on CTRL the full-scale 100mV threshold applies. Below 1V the threshold scales with CTRL, down to zero LED current, with relative accuracy falling as the threshold shrinks. This widens the total dimming range by a factor of ten. CTRL can be fed from a thermistor divider for LED overtemperature foldback, or from a divider on VIN to cut power at low input; tie it to VREF if unused.

RLED in series with the LEDs is Kelvin-sensed by ISP and ISN, normally at the top of the string. Sensing at the bottom is possible if ISN never drops below 3V, the lower limit of LED current regulation. Switching-frequency ripple across ISP–ISN is normal and is averaged by the VC capacitor; ripple above 20mV peak-to-peak does not upset operation but can offset the average from the set value. Ripple grows with LED current and falls with frequency and output capacitance.

operation.topic: Voltage loop, open LED and overvoltage
operation.text: FB is compared with a 1.25V reference and can take over the loop, which gives constant-voltage operation and limits the output when the LEDs open. FB within 50mV (–4%) of regulation turns on the OPENLED pull-down on LT3755 and LT3755-2. FB 60mV (5% typ) above regulation drives PWMOUT low regardless of PWM, so a disconnect NFET isolates the LEDs from GND. Grounding FB disables the voltage loop; tying ISP to ISN and CTRL to VREF disables the current loop.

If an external event forces FB above both the open-LED and overvoltage (1.31V typ) thresholds, OPENLED releases. The LT3755-2 asserts it again as soon as FB comes back below 1.31V while still above the open-LED threshold. The LT3755 keeps it released until FB drops below the 1.2V (typ) open-LED threshold and the fault clears. The LT3755-2 behaviour is the general-purpose choice where OPENLED is used. With the clamp set so that FB stays at or below 1.1V with LEDs connected, FB within 50mV of 1.25V means an open LED.

RT to GND sets 100kHz to 1MHz (Table 1); the pin must not be left open. Higher frequency shrinks the magnetics but raises switching loss and gate drive current and narrows the usable duty-cycle range; lower frequency is more efficient with larger parts. The minimum on- and off-times bound the duty cycle at a given frequency.

SYNC locks the switching frequency to an external clock; set RT 20% below the clock frequency. SYNC is ignored during soft-start. A 50% duty-cycle clock is preferred; otherwise keep it between 20% and 60%. Using PWM and SYNC together, PWM should rise at least 200ns before the SYNC rising edge. Ground SYNC when unused.

INTVCC needs a capacitor for stability and to supply the gate current pulses: a 10V, low-ESR X7R or X5R ceramic, 4.7µF for most designs, placed close to the INTVCC pin and IC ground. Its current limit protects the IC from dissipation at high VIN, so QG at 7V times the frequency must stay below it. INTVCC has its own 4.1V (typ) undervoltage lockout: below it GATE and PWMOUT are forced to 0V and soft-start resets. With VIN never above 8V, INTVCC can be tied to VIN, which allows operation down to 4.5V and adds under 12µA of shutdown load on INTVCC. If VIN is normally higher but sometimes dips below the INTVCC regulation voltage, the minimum operating VIN is close to 6V, set by the regulator dropout and the INTVCC lockout.

The 1.22V falling threshold on SHDN/UVLO is set accurately by a divider from VIN; below it a 2.1µA pull-down adds hysteresis set by the upper resistor. Pulling the pin to 0.4V or less shuts the part down with VIN current below 1µA.

The SS capacitor charges from 10µA, lowering the oscillator frequency and the switch current limit while it rises, which cuts inrush and output overshoot. Three events empty it: SHDN/UVLO dropping under its threshold, overtemperature, and INTVCC undervoltage. When starting from SHDN/UVLO, SS begins charging after the first PWM high period.

At a junction temperature of 165°C GATE and PWMOUT are pulled to GND and SS is discharged; switching resumes once the die has cooled by 10°C. Most of the IC dissipation is the gate drive current, so use a low-QG MOSFET and a suitable frequency at high VIN, keeping TJ under 125°C (150°C for H grade). Solder the exposed pad to a ground plane tied to inner copper with thermal vias under the package.

Below ISN = 3V, outside the LED sensing common-mode range (start-up or a shorted output), the ISP/ISN pair keeps measuring current and blocks switch turn-on while the difference exceeds 150mV (typ). This sits above the 100mV regulation threshold so the two functions do not conflict where they overlap. With an inductive load, the SEPIC should have a Schottky clamp (anode GND, cathode ISN) to limit current out of ISN during a fault.

The input capacitor carries the inductor's transient input current; X7R ceramic is preferred for its stability over temperature and bias. Boost and SEPIC need less input capacitance than buck mode. In buck mode the input capacitor sees large pulsed currents through the Schottky, so place it right at the diode and at the sense-resistor ground return, and choose low ESR and ESL with an adequate ripple-current rating.

The output capacitor filters LED ripple current, since the LED's equivalent resistance is low; X7R ceramics are advised. For equal LED ripple, boost and buck-boost mode need more capacitance than buck mode, and lower frequencies need proportionally more.

At high input or output voltage the switch is chosen for VDS rating and low QG; RDS(ON) matters less because switching losses dominate. The VDS rating must exceed the open-LED clamp set by FB. The MOSFETs in the application circuits are known to work with the LT3755.
Rate the diode for the maximum switch-node voltage. With PWM dimming, its reverse leakage, which rises with temperature, discharges the output during PWM low, so pick a low-leakage part.

RSENSE from the MOSFET source to GND must allow the needed switch current without reaching the 108mV (typ) limit; the RSENSE equations assume typical ripple, and higher ripple (current-limited high duty cycle, discontinuous conduction) needs a lower value. Check the peak inductor current in the circuit. Place RSENSE close to the MOSFET source and the IC GND, with SENSE Kelvin-connected to its positive end.
Choose saturation current above the maximum switch current set by RSENSE, and an inductance that makes the SENSE voltage ramp by about 20mV over each on-time.

The VC network, the inductor and the output capacitor set loop stability. For typical LED designs 2.2nF on VC is enough; always add a series resistor so VC can slew faster and hold the LED current tighter through fast input transients.

The exposed pad is the only GND connection and the main heat path, so bond it well to the ground plane. Keep the high dV/dt switch node (inductor, MOSFET drain, Schottky anode) small, with a ground plane under it. Keep short the two high dI/dt loops: switch node through MOSFET and RSENSE to GND, and switch node through the Schottky and output capacitor to GND; join their grounds at one point and then to the plane under the IC. Put the INTVCC capacitor ground near the switching ground; this usually places the MOSFET and INTVCC capacitor nearest the IC. Star-connect the compensation and other DC control grounds under the IC. Keep FB and VC traces short, do not run FB beside PWMOUT for more than a few millimetres, and keep series resistance out of the SENSE line.
